doc.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Jazz Forum and the school he ran on 8th Avenue
summary: He worked at the Jazz Forum, then with partners opened a place on 8th Avenue where he taught for five years.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: So this place, Jazz Forum – Jazz at the Forum that you were connected to, that recently had that celebration at Lincoln Center, that’s thirty years…
Oh that was – just to run the place, that was…
When you first came to New York, you were?

I mean, I was – I worked there, the Jazz Forum. Duo worked there, Tommy Flannigan. You know, we all worked at that place. See, Jazz Forum was one of those places where we did have a chance to work. Um, but then – after that, I opened a place. Jazz Forum closed – me and Larry Ridley, and a couple more people, Jim Harrison and Fuente, we opened a place on 8th avenue. So we opened a place on 8th avenue, so I taught there. Caught the devil, but that’s where I taught.
Paying the rent. We had to pay 3,000 dollars a month to pay the rent, that ain’t no joke.
Oh, 8th avenue. And what was the cross street, about?
Between 28th and 29th. So I had that place.
Five years. It lasted five years. I refused to close it. I could have refused to pay the tent and just forget it, but um, I lasted for five whole years. With the help of people. I
had help from a couple of people, you know. And um, it was a good thing, ‘cause people still go there asking for that place – Japanese.
